<result>Reviewed PR #99 (`agent/fix-head-source-provenance`, 7 files, +421/-20) against `origin/main`. I checked out the branch in a scratch worktree, read every hunk with surrounding context, traced the provenance chain end-to-end (`prepareSource` → `openSource` → `restampCachedSearchSnapshotCommit` → `Header.Commit`), built the binary, and exercised `--head` on synthetic repos (no commits, dirty tree, file deleted in worktree, JSON/bad-format paths). `go vet ./internal/cli`, the new tests, and the full `internal/cli` suite all pass.

Note: no `ReportFindings` tool is exposed in this session (I searched for it twice), so findings are reported inline below.

## Verdict

The core change is sound. The provenance gate (`worktree || snapshot.Header.Commit == ""`) is correct in every path I could construct:

- `--head` on a repo with no HEAD → `resolveCommittedHEAD` returns `("", "", err)`, `Header.Commit` is empty, the reader correctly falls back to disk (verified live — `E_NO_GIT_HEAD` warning, working-tree bodies).
- A worktree snapshot always carries `Header.Commit` set to HEAD, but the `worktree` flag is checked first, so it never routes to git.
- Tree-only cache keying is safe here because `restampCachedSearchSnapshotCommit` is applied on every cache-hit return path reachable from `LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot`, so the commit used as a treeish is always the serving HEAD — never a dangling one.
- The new reader mirrors `internal/sem/provider.go:9764` (`openSource`) exactly — same `BatchFileReader`, same `ShowFile` newline escape hatch, same 4 MiB cap — so path semantics and size cutoffs match the reader that produced the snapshot's symbols. Notably `defaultMaxParseBytes` and `callSiteMaxFileBytes` are both 4 MiB, so an oversized blob can never be requested for a file that was parsed.
- No other CLI verb was left behind: after the change, the only production callers of the on-disk `newRepoLineReader` are the `openSnapshotLineReader` fallback itself; `explain` reads no source (snapshot signatures only, so the header-only fix is the right scope), and `search` already handles `--head` in `internal/sem/search.go:783`.

## Findings (4, all low)

- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/callsite.go:91` — a `NewBatchFileReader` failure is now fatal to the whole command. `runDef`/`runNeighbors`/`runImpact` return the error, so a fork/fd-exhaustion failure turns a `--head` query that previously printed the complete graph answer (minus source windows) into no output at all. Source enrichment is a presentation nicety everywhere else in this file — `symbolMatchBodiesFromReader` and `resolveCallSite` both degrade silently on an unreadable file. Suggest degrading to a reader that always reports `false` (no source, no dirty source) rather than aborting.
- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/def.go:176` — the reader is opened before the format switch, so `def --head --format json` spawns and tears down a `git cat-file --batch` child that `writeDefBodiesFromReader` never touches (verified: the JSON path works, but the process is pure overhead). It also adds the spawn cost to `index_latency_ms`, which is measured at line 182 after the open. Same ordering in `impact.go:150` and `neighbors.go:163`, though those two do use the reader in the JSON path.
- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/explain.go:191` — provenance was made explicit only for `text`/`agent`. `ExplainResponse` (line 102) carries no commit/tree/worktree field, so `explain --head --format json` and `explain --format json` are byte-identical on a clean tree and a machine consumer still cannot tell which tree the declarations came from. Schema is additive-only, so a `commit`/`tree` field would close the gap the text renderer just closed.
- `/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/def.go:230` — `writeDefBodies`, `buildNeighborResponse` (`neighbors.go:333`), `buildImpactResponse` (`impact.go:333`) and `symbolMatchBodies` (`symbolref.go:628`) are now test-only shims that hardwire the on-disk reader. The large existing suites (`neighbors_efficiency_test.go`, `impact_test.go`, `symbolref_test.go`) all still call the legacy wrappers, so the production `*FromReader` path is covered only by the new file — future regressions in the wired-up path can pass CI. Worth pointing the existing tests at the `FromReader` forms and dropping the shims.</result>

content.text:
Merge it, with one fix first.

**Fix before merge — `internal/cli/callsite.go:91`.** It's the only finding that changes behavior for a user. Degrade a failed `NewBatchFileReader` to a reader that reports "no source" instead of returning the error up through `runDef`/`runNeighbors`/`runImpact`. That matches how the rest of that file already treats unreadable source, and it keeps a `--head` query answering the graph question when git can't spawn. Small, contained change.

**Fold in cheaply if you're touching it anyway — `internal/cli/def.go:176`.** Move the reader open inside the format switch so the JSON path doesn't spawn a `git cat-file` child it never reads. Two-line move; also stops it skewing `index_latency_ms`.

18	// A CALLS relation records, as evidence, the span of the CALLER'S BODY — not the
19	// line the call is written on. Reporting that span's first line as the caller's
20	// location is the single most expensive inaccuracy a relation answer can carry:
21	// on a long dispatch function it points thousands of lines away from the call,
22	// and the reader has to go find it. The definition line is still reported, but
23	// the primary location is now the call itself.
24	//
25	// The call line is recovered from the source rather than from the parser, so
26	// this stays entirely inside the relation-output layer: the caller's body span
27	// is known, the call expression's text is known (evidence detail), and the file
28	// comes from the same source view as the graph. Everything below is
29	// deterministic and language-agnostic.
30	
31	const (
32		// callContextGuardLimit caps how many enclosing block headers are quoted.
33		// Six covers the deepest real dispatch nesting seen in practice while
34		// keeping the block far cheaper than the caller's body.
35		callContextGuardLimit = 6
36		// callContextWindowLines is the size of the verbatim window around a call.
37		callContextWindowLines = 10
38		// callContextBlocks caps how many callers get a source window. Reporting
39		// the LINE is unconditional and costs ~4 bytes; quoting source is not.
40		callContextBlocks = 3
41		// callContextBudget is the total byte ceiling for all quoted call context in
42		// one answer. A window is ~100x cheaper than the caller body it replaces, so
43		// this is generous, but it must still be bounded.
44		callContextBudget = 2000
45		// callContextLineWidth truncates a quoted line. Machine-generated source can
46		// carry multi-kilobyte lines that would blow the budget on one entry.
47		callContextLineWidth = 160
48		// callSiteMaxFileBytes bounds the file read behind call-site resolution.
49		callSiteMaxFileBytes = 4 << 20
50		// callSiteHeaderLookback is how far above an opening brace the statement
51		// that owns it may start (`if cond\n  && other\n{`).
52		callSiteHeaderLookback = 6
53	)
54	
55	// callSite is the concrete location of a call inside a caller's body.
56	type callSite struct {
57		FilePath string `json:"file_path"`
58		Line     int    `json:"line"`
59		// AdditionalSites counts further call sites of the same callee in the same
60		// caller, so a reader knows one line is not the whole story.
61		AdditionalSites int `json:"additional_sites,omitempty"`
62		// Guards are the enclosing block headers in force at the call, outermost
63		// first: the `if let` / `match` / `else if` chain a patch has to stay
64		// correct under. Verbatim source lines, never a synthesized claim.
65		Guards []sourceLine `json:"guards,omitempty"`
66		// GuardsOmitted counts enclosing block headers dropped by the guard cap, so
67		// a truncated chain is never presented as the whole chain.
68		GuardsOmitted int `json:"outer_guards_omitted,omitempty"`
69		// Window is the verbatim source around the call. Excluded from JSON: a JSON
70		// consumer has the line number and the file.
71		Window      []sourceLine `json:"-"`
72		WindowStart int          `json:"-"`
73		WindowEnd   int          `json:"-"`
74	}
75	
76	// sourceLine is one numbered, verbatim line of source.
77	type sourceLine struct {
78		Line int    `json:"line"`
79		Text string `json:"text"`
80	}
81	
82	// lineReader returns a repo-relative file's lines. Missing/unreadable/binary
83	// files report false; callers degrade to the definition line.
84	type lineReader func(relPath string) ([]string, bool)
85	
86	// openSnapshotLineReader returns one memoized source reader whose provenance
87	// matches snapshot. A committed snapshot must never be annotated with dirty
88	// working-tree source, so --head reads through one command-lifetime git
89	// cat-file process bound to the snapshot's commit. Worktree snapshots, and the
90	// provider's no-HEAD fallback, keep the contained on-disk reader.
91	func openSnapshotLineReader(
92		ctx context.Context,
93		snapshot sem.ProviderSnapshot,
94		worktree bool,
95	) (lineReader, func() error, error) {
96		if worktree || snapshot.Header.Commit == "" {
97			return newRepoLineReader(snapshot.Header.RepoRoot), nil, nil
98		}
99	
100		batch, err := gitutil.NewBatchFileReader(ctx, snapshot.Header.RepoRoot, snapshot.Header.Commit)
101		if err != nil {
102			return nil, nil, err
103		}
104		batch.SetMaxBytes(callSiteMaxFileBytes)
105	
106		cache := map[string][]string{}
107		read := func(relPath string) ([]string, bool) {
108			if relPath == "" || snapshot.Header.RepoRoot == "" {
109				return nil, false
110			}
111			if lines, ok := cache[relPath]; ok {
112				return lines, lines != nil
113			}
114	
115			var content string
116			var ok bool
117			var readErr error
118			if strings.Contains(relPath, "\n") {
119				// The batch protocol is line based, so a newline-bearing Git path
120				// needs the argv-safe one-shot reader. It still reads the same commit;
121				// failure never falls back to the dirty working tree.
122				content, ok, readErr = gitutil.ShowFile(ctx, snapshot.Header.RepoRoot, snapshot.Header.Commit, relPath)
123				if int64(len(content)) > callSiteMaxFileBytes {
124					ok = false
125				}
126			} else {
127				content, ok, readErr = batch.ReadFile(relPath)
128			}
129			if readErr != nil || !ok || strings.IndexByte(content, 0) >= 0 {
130				cache[relPath] = nil
131				return nil, false
132			}
133	
134			lines := strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n")
135			cache[relPath] = lines
136			return lines, true
137		}
138		return read, batch.Close, nil
139	}

141	// newRepoLineReader reads files under repoRoot, memoizing per path so several
142	// call sites in one file cost one read. It refuses oversized and NUL-bearing
143	// files: neither can usefully be quoted.
144	//
145	// repoRoot is a boundary, not a prefix. Reads go through os.Root, so a relPath
146	// containing `..`, an absolute path, or a component that is a symlink pointing
147	// outside the tree cannot resolve to a file the caller did not mean to expose.
148	// filepath.Join alone gave none of that: it happily normalizes `../secret` into
149	// a path above the root, and os.Lstat only guarded the FINAL component, so an
150	// intermediate symlink was followed by the subsequent read.
151	//
152	// Nothing reaches this with an untrusted relPath today — callers pass paths
153	// from a snapshot this process built, and both snapshot sources omit
154	// symlinks. That is a property of today's callers, held by nothing: the
155	// signature takes any string, and this package already ships a verb that
156	// ingests externally supplied snapshot records. Making the boundary structural
157	// costs one syscall per distinct file and removes the question.
158	func newRepoLineReader(repoRoot string) lineReader {
159		cache := map[string][]string{}
160		return func(relPath string) ([]string, bool) {
161			if relPath == "" || repoRoot == "" {
162				return nil, false
163			}
164			if lines, ok := cache[relPath]; ok {
165				return lines, lines != nil
166			}
167			lines, ok := readRepoFileLines(repoRoot, relPath)
168			if !ok {
169				cache[relPath] = nil
170				return nil, false
171			}
172			cache[relPath] = lines
173			return lines, true
174		}
175	}
176	
177	// readRepoFileLines performs one contained read. It is separate from the memo so
178	// the containment can be tested without reasoning about cache state.
179	func readRepoFileLines(repoRoot, relPath string) ([]string, bool) {

181		if err != nil {
182			return nil, false
183		}
184		defer root.Close()

187		// so containment is the only behavior this function changes. Root.Lstat does
188		// not traverse the link, and Root.Open would not leave the root anyway.

17	// explain — turn a FAILING BUILD into the declarations it is complaining about.
18	//
19	// Why this exists, measured on a 30-instance paired haiku run (baseline vs graph-assisted, same
20	// instances, same prompt discipline):
21	//
22	//	                  baseline    graph
23	//	pre-edit explore     9.43      1.34    <- the locate phase is already won, 86% removed
24	//	post-edit explore    8.60      6.76    <- barely moved
25	//	post-edit read       3.57      4.07    <- moved the WRONG way
26	//	verify/fix total    17.57     16.17    <- 50% of the assisted session, -7.9%
27	//
28	// The graph has taken essentially everything available in the locate phase; half of what remains is
29	// the edit->build->fix loop, and the graph did nothing for it. The reason is not that the graph lacks
30	// the answer — `def` has it — but that the agent never asks: offering `def` in the prompt for exactly
31	// this case produced 0.04 calls per session across 28 sessions. Telling an agent to choose a tool
32	// after its build fails does not work; it is already in the shell, so it greps.
33	//
34	// So this is not another instruction. It is a command that composes with the build in ONE shell call,
35	// and the VERIFY block emits it pre-composed, so the agent runs the command it was given and the
36	// declarations arrive with the failure:
37	//
38	//	go test ./internal/configs -run '^TestX$' 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .
39	//
40	// One turn replaces build -> grep symbol -> read range. It quotes no source it was not asked for and
41	// it stays read-only: the build is run by the shell, not by this process, so the provider remains a
42	// pure analyzer.
43	const (
44		// explainMaxSymbols bounds how many distinct names are resolved. A cascading build failure can
45		// name hundreds; the first few are the cause and the rest are consequences.
46		explainMaxSymbols = 8
47	
48		// explainMaxBytes bounds the whole block, on the same reasoning as the search payload: bytes here
49		// are replayed into the model on every later turn.
50		explainMaxBytes = 2048
51	)
52	
53	// explainErrorPatterns are the ways compilers and test runners name a symbol they cannot resolve.
54	// Each pattern captures ONE identifier. They are deliberately conservative: a pattern that also
55	// matched ordinary prose would fill the block with words that are not symbols, which is strictly
56	// worse than an empty block.
57	var explainErrorPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
58		// Go: "undefined: foo", "x.foo undefined (type T has no field or method foo)"
59		regexp.MustCompile(`undefined:\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)`),
60		regexp.MustCompile(`has no field or method\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
61		regexp.MustCompile(`declared and not used:\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
62		// Rust: "cannot find function `foo`", "no method named `foo`", "unresolved import `a::b`"
63		regexp.MustCompile("cannot find (?:function|value|type|struct|trait|macro)[^`]*`([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
64		regexp.MustCompile("no method named `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
65		regexp.MustCompile("no field `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
66		// Java / Kotlin: "cannot find symbol\n  symbol: method foo(int)"
67		regexp.MustCompile(`symbol:\s+(?:method|variable|class)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),

content.text:
All four findings are addressed.

**PR #99** — the two pre-merge fixes are pushed (`9ad5da6`):
- `openSnapshotLineReaderOrDegrade` replaces the fatal open in `def`/`neighbors`/`impact`. A failed `git cat-file --batch` spawn now costs the answer its source windows, not the answer, and warns on stderr. New test builds the reader against a nonexistent repo root to force the failure.
- `def` opens the reader only for `text`/`agent`. Verified with a `git` shim counting spawns on a warm cache: `--format json` went 1 → 0, `text` stays at 1 and still uses it.

**New PRs**, both stacked on `agent/fix-head-source-provenance` (GitHub retargets them to main when #99 merges):
- **#107** — https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/107 — drops the shims. `writeDefBodies` had no callers at all and is deleted; the other three become `*OnDisk` helpers in a `_test.go` file, so no test-only path ships in the binary and each call site names its reader. Adds `TestNeighborsJSONCallSitesFollowSelectedTree`, mutation-checked by forcing the on-disk reader — it fails with `call site at line 8, want the committed line 7`.

`gofmt`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass on all three branches.

One judgment call worth flagging: I left `index_latency_ms` measured after the reader open in all three verbs rather than moving it. It slightly overstates index time for the source-quoting formats, but keeping the three verbs consistent seemed better than fixing it in `def` alone. Say the word if you'd rather have it moved everywhere.

content.text:
Here's the full shape of it.

**What the number currently measures.** In all three verbs the sequence is: start clock → `LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot` → open the source reader → *stop* the index clock → start the query clock. So `index_latency_ms` spans snapshot load **plus** the `git cat-file --batch` spawn (`def.go:187`, `impact.go:154`, `neighbors.go:167`). The reader open isn't indexing — it's output setup — so the field slightly overstates what its name claims.

**Magnitude.** A `git cat-file --batch` spawn+teardown measures ~10.7 ms in a shell loop here (real in-process cost is somewhat lower — that figure includes the shell's own fork). Against a cold index, seconds long, it's noise. Against a *warm* `--head` run it isn't: `def --symbol Caller --head` on a cache hit reports `index_latency_ms=23, query=0, total=23`. So on exactly the runs people benchmark — and the ones the statusline badge reports — the spawn is a visible fraction of the number.

**Why I left it.** Three reasons, in order of weight:

1. Fixing it only in `def` — where the actual waste was — would make the three verbs disagree about what `index_latency_ms` includes. A consistent small overstatement beats an inconsistent one; anyone comparing `neighbors` to `def` timings would be comparing different quantities.
2. It's a semantics change to user-visible telemetry, not a bug fix. If anyone is tracking these numbers across runs, the series shifts under them. That deserves its own PR and its own line in the changelog, not a silent ride-along in a PR about source provenance.
3. The obvious fix has a wrinkle. Move `indexLatency := time.Since(indexStarted)` up to just after the snapshot load, and the reader open now falls *between* the index stop and the query start — counted in neither, so `index + query < total` with an unexplained gap. To avoid that you'd also move `queryStarted := time.Now()` above the open, attributing the spawn to query latency. That's defensible (it is work done to answer this query) but it's a second arbitrary choice, and I didn't want to make two of those unilaterally.

**If you want it changed**, the shape I'd pick: one small PR touching all three verbs, stopping the index clock immediately after `LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot` and starting the query clock in the same breath, so the reader open lands in query time and no time goes unattributed.

One thing that cuts both ways: nothing pins the current composition. The only assertion anywhere is `neighbors_efficiency_test.go:54` checking `total >= index` and `total >= query`, and no doc defines the fields. So the change is safe to make — and equally, nothing would have caught it if #99 had shifted these numbers by accident. If we do touch it, that PR should add the assertion that's missing.

## Root cause

The graph snapshot respected `--head`, but several CLI presentation paths reopened files from disk afterward. A dirty working tree could therefore combine committed symbols and relations with uncommitted bodies, guards, windows, or line numbers.

## User impact

Explicit `--head` queries now return graph facts and displayed source from the same committed revision. The default agent workflow remains working-tree-first and is unchanged; this PR does not modify the README.

## Validation

- `mise run check` (format, vet, race tests, build, and status-line tests)
- `mise exec -- go test ./internal/cli -count=1`
- independent read-only diff review

content.text:
Both reviews are in, on `9ad5da6`.

**Cursor Bugbot** — no issues found.

**Copilot** — summary plus one inline finding, [`internal/cli/callsite.go:128`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/99), and it's a real one:

> the committed-tree reader falls back to `gitutil.ShowFile()`, which currently captures the entire blob into memory with no read-side size bound

I checked it against the two sibling paths, and the asymmetry is exactly as described:

- on-disk reader (`callsite.go:220`): `Lstat` size check, then `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(file, max+1))` — bounded *before* materializing, with a comment explaining it doesn't trust the stat because the file can grow between calls.
- batch reader (`gitutil/git.go:662`): reads the size from the `cat-file` header and streams oversized blobs to `io.Discard` — never materializes.
- the new newline-path branch: `ShowFile` → `runWithStderr`, which buffers all of stdout into a `bytes.Buffer` (`git.go:777`), and only then does `if int64(len(content)) > callSiteMaxFileBytes { ok = false }`. The cap is enforced after the allocation, not before.

**My read on severity: low, but worth fixing.** Reaching it needs a Git path containing a literal newline *and* a blob far over 4 MiB. For paths from a snapshot this process built that's near-contradictory — a file that big wouldn't have been parsed, so it wouldn't have symbols to read source for. The vector that isn't contradictory is the one `newRepoLineReader`'s own comment already names: this package ships a verb that ingests externally supplied snapshot records, so the path can be attacker-chosen. That's precisely why the on-disk reader was made structurally bounded rather than bounded-by-caller-discipline. The git-backed reader should hold the same line.

The fix is a size-limited variant in `gitutil` — stream `git show` stdout through an `io.LimitReader` instead of buffering it — and call that from the newline branch. Contained, and it needs a test with an oversized newline-named blob.

Want me to add it to #99, or open it as a third follow-up PR?

Second round on `c645ae2` — both clean.

**Cursor Bugbot** — no issues.

**Copilot** — 9/9 files, no new comments. It did log one *suppressed* comment (its own low-confidence bucket) on `internal/gitutil/git.go:571`:

> If `maxBytes` is near int64 max, `maxBytes+1` can overflow to a negative limit, causing `ReadAll` to return immediately and `cmd.Wait()` to potentially deadlock while git is still writing to stdout.

I traced it, and the mechanism is right. At exactly `math.MaxInt64` the `+1` wraps negative; `io.LimitReader` returns EOF immediately when `N <= 0`, so `content` is empty, `oversized` is `0 > MaxInt64` = false, and we skip the `cancel()`. Two outcomes from there: a blob smaller than the 64 KiB pipe buffer returns empty content as `ok=true` (silently wrong), and a larger one hangs — git blocks writing to a pipe nobody is draining, `cmd.Wait()` never returns, and the `defer cancel()` that would break it is behind that Wait.

It needs `maxBytes == math.MaxInt64` exactly. The only caller passes `callSiteMaxFileBytes` (4 MiB), so it's unreachable today — which is presumably why Copilot suppressed it. The counter-argument is the one this codebase already makes for `newRepoLineReader`: the signature accepts any value and nothing holds the constraint. The guard is two lines — treat an overflowing `+1` as "no ceiling" and fall through to `ShowFile`.

Want me to add it, or leave #99 as is? Both bots are green either way.

content.text:
Checked this rather than assumed — three things determine the answer.

**No effect on retrieval recall.** The recall numbers in `docs/benchmarks.md` (LOCOMO recall@10) come from `graph search`, which lives in `internal/sem`. None of the three PRs touches that package — the diffs are confined to `internal/cli` plus `internal/gitutil/git.go`. The readers involved are `internal/cli`-private, so `sem` cannot reach them even in principle.

**The reader can't change what's found, only what's quoted.** In `buildNeighborResponseFromReader` and its impact twin, resolution finishes before `readSource` is consumed: `resolveFocusSymbolsOrFuzzy` → sort → truncate, all independent of the reader. `readSource` then feeds exactly two things — `symbolMatchBodiesFromReader` (`neighbors.go:395`, `impact.go:395`) and `annotate*CallSites`. In `def` it feeds only `writeDefBodiesFromReader`. So a reader that returns nothing costs source windows, never symbols, relations, or ranking.

**Where something does change** — call it source-context recall, what an agent gets in one turn:

1. **The degraded path is new information loss.** If the `git cat-file` child can't spawn under `--head`, the answer now arrives with locations but no bodies, call-site lines, guards, or windows — so the agent pays a follow-up Read. That's strictly better than the two alternatives it replaced (mid-#99: the whole command failed; pre-#99: source was quoted from the wrong tree), and it warns on stderr, but it is a real reduction in a rare failure mode.
2. **`--head` on a dirty tree quotes committed source by design.** An agent that just edited files and passes `--head` no longer sees its own edits in the quoted bodies. That is the fix — internally consistent instead of mixed — but it does change what comes back. The default worktree path is untouched.
3. Ambiguous/fuzzy match bodies under `--head` read from the commit too, with no loss: a symbol absent from the commit isn't in a `--head` snapshot to begin with.

**If you meant speed rather than retrieval quality:** `--head` source reads now go through one `cat-file --batch` child per command (~5–10 ms spawn, amortized across every file the answer touches) instead of direct `os` reads — cheaper across many files, marginally more for one. `def --format json` got strictly faster, one fewer spawn. Indexing and search latency are untouched. #106 adds a few dozen bytes to `explain` JSON; #107 is behavior-identical in production.

Git authorship doesn't separate them — every commit carries your identity, since the original PR was produced in your environment too. The boundary is the commit: `3c0c312` is the original PR; the three on top are this session.

**Original author (`3c0c312`, 421 insertions):**
- the whole mechanism — `openSnapshotLineReader`, the git-backed committed reader, threading it through `def`/`neighbors`/`impact`, `symbolMatchBodiesFromReader`, the `explain` text header

- caveat 3 — ambiguous-match bodies read from the commit
- the `cat-file` child per `--head` command, i.e. the latency change
- also the two defects that came out of review: the fatal open failure, and the unbounded newline-path read

**This session (`9ad5da6`, `c645ae2`, `ad05a48`, 294 insertions):**
- **caveat 1 is mine.** The degraded path — locations without quoted source — did not exist before `9ad5da6`. The original behavior on a failed spawn was to fail the whole command, so this replaced a total loss with a partial one, but the specific behavior I described as information loss is a thing I introduced.
- `def --format json` skipping the reader open
- `gitutil.ShowFileLimited` and the bounded newline-path read, from Copilot's finding

One of those deserves to be called out rather than folded into the list: **`ad05a48` fixes a bug that `c645ae2` introduced.** The `maxBytes+1` overflow Copilot caught existed only because my `ShowFileLimited` created it — the original code had no such arithmetic. Two of the three review-driven commits are mine fixing the author's work; the third is mine fixing my own.

PRs **#106** and **#107** are entirely this session's work, both derived from findings rather than from the original PR's scope.

536	// ShowFileLimited is ShowFile with a READ-SIDE ceiling: it never materializes
537	// more than maxBytes+1 of the blob, and reports a larger blob as unreadable.
538	//
539	// ShowFile buffers all of git's stdout before returning, so a caller that only
540	// wants small files could not express that: checking len(content) afterwards
541	// enforces the ceiling on the ANSWER while the allocation has already happened.
542	// Every other bounded read in this package refuses before materializing — the
543	// batch reader streams an oversized blob to io.Discard off its header size, and
544	// the on-disk reader reads through an io.LimitReader — so this closes the one
545	// path where the bound arrived too late.
546	//
547	// The over-limit blob is not drained: cancelling the context stops git instead,
548	// because the bytes were already refused and reading them to /dev/null is the
549	// same wait this ceiling exists to avoid.
550	func ShowFileLimited(ctx context.Context, repo, rev, path string, maxBytes int64) (string, bool, error) {
551		// The read is bounded at maxBytes+1 so that "exceeded" is distinguishable
552		// from "exactly at the ceiling". At math.MaxInt64 that wraps negative, and a
553		// negative io.LimitReader EOFs at once: the blob would read as empty and the
554		// oversize test could not fire, leaving git blocked on a pipe nobody drains
555		// while Wait blocks on git. A ceiling no blob can reach is no ceiling, so it
556		// takes the unbounded path instead.
557		limit := maxBytes + 1
558		if maxBytes <= 0 || limit <= 0 {
559			return ShowFile(ctx, repo, rev, path)
560		}
561		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
562		defer cancel()
563	
564		// Same object spec and the same stderr-only classification as ShowFile; see
565		// there for why the revision is peeled to a tree first.

572			return "", false, err
573		}

581		}
582		waitErr := cmd.Wait()
583		switch {

content.text:
Two Windows failures, and the important one was mine. Fixed in `0704f56`, CI re-running.

**`internal/gitutil` — 10-minute timeout, introduced by me in `c645ae2`.** `ShowFileLimited` hung in `Cmd.Wait` → `awaitGoroutines`. Reading through an `io.LimitReader` and cancelling git once the ceiling is passed depends on process-tree teardown: killing git left a grandchild holding the inherited stderr handle, so the copier goroutine feeding my `bytes.Buffer` never saw EOF and `Wait` blocked forever. It passed locally on macOS and I shipped it without a Windows signal.

It now asks `git cat-file -s` for the blob size and refuses before reading a byte — the shape both sibling readers already have (batch decides off its header, on-disk stats before opening). Nothing depends on killing a process, and the `maxBytes+1` arithmetic that needed `ad05a48`'s overflow guard is gone with it. Verified `cat-file -s` emits the identical missing-path diagnostic as `git show`, so absent stays absent; both existing tests still pass, including the 167 MB→<4 MiB allocation assertion.

**`internal/cli` — `TestHeadSnapshotLineReaderPreservesCommittedFileContract`, pre-existing.** It fails on Windows since the original `3c0c312`, not from anything this session did: the fixture creates a file whose *name* contains a newline, which Windows cannot do. I skipped only that case rather than the test — CRLF handling, NUL rejection, the size ceiling and worktree isolation are all cross-platform and still asserted.

Worth being straight about the process failure here: I ran `go test ./...` locally after every change and reported it as passing, which it was — on macOS. I never looked at the PR's checks until you asked, so a hang I introduced sat in CI across two of my own review rounds while I reported the PR as green from the bots.
